title: A spare elsewhere changes the gap
hook: Two here, five freely available there: how many new units are missing?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Account for transferable surplus before computing external replenishment.

misconception: Only items already in the destination count toward its shortage.
objective: Account for transferable surplus before computing external replenishment.

claims.text: There are two usable local units and five uncommitted units elsewhere that can be transferred at zero modeled cost. Scaled model; transfer allowed; zero modeled transfer cost.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Required=10, A=8items and B=3items. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",2]]; B=["max",0,["-","x",7]]; x denotes Required. At x=10, A=8, B=3; recall at x=13: B=6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Pooling available stock changes the shortage from requirement minus two to requirement minus seven. The result depends on those other units actually being free and transferable under the stated assumptions.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. claims.text: There are two usable local units and five uncommitted units elsewhere that can be transferred at zero modeled cost. Change only Required to 13. What is B (Pooled) now? Correct: 6items. Use B's stated rule with Required=13: it gives 6items. Pooling available stock changes the shortage from requirement minus two to requirement minus seven. The result depends on those other units actually being free and transferable under the stated assumptions.

recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Required=13: it gives 6items. Pooling available stock changes the shortage from requirement minus two to requirement minus seven. The result depends on those other units actually being free and transferable under the stated assumptions.
